requirements_trace.claim: A cut-over host must refuse the canonical-local ~/.sirsi/router.db even when a future dashboard/native integration tries to bypass Resolve, using the existing keystone rather than a second store.
evidence: TestResolveRefusesExplicitSIRSIRouterDBWhenItNamesTheCanonicalLedgerOnACutOverHost: negative control -- SIRSI_ROUTER_DB explicitly set to ~/.sirsi/router.db on a cut-over host (router-service.env present) still self-heals to *RemoteStore and never opens/creates the canonical local file

TestResolveStillHonorsSIRSIRouterDBForAGenuinelyDifferentPathOnACutOverHost: positive control -- SIRSI_ROUTER_DB naming a genuinely different path still bypasses the cut-over check and opens *SQLiteStore directly
No production code changed: reuses internal/routerstore/resolve.go's existing cutOverMarker/samePath keystone (ADR-069), does not introduce a second store abstraction

closure_evidence.technical: Traced codex's 'Resolve'/'keystone' reference to internal/routerstore/resolve.go's cutOverMarker (its own comment names it 'the keystone', ADR-069). That function already special-cases an explicit SIRSI_ROUTER_DB naming the canonical ~/.sirsi/router.db on a cut-over host (must not bypass), but no test exercised that branch -- existing coverage (resolve_cutover_test.go) only ever set SIRSI_ROUTER_DB to a different path. Added the missing negative control paired with a positive control, both calling the real Resolve() entry point.
closure_evidence.operational: PR #939 opened against main, pushed through the Ma'at pre-push gate (gitleaks clean, go test -race ./internal/routerstore green under host load), CI triggered; sent to codex-pantheon for independent review+bind per A34 since this is self-authored
closure_evidence.narrative: Closes the test-coverage gap on the ra-fabric-canonical-local-refusal task; the production refusal mechanism already existed and was already correct, this closure proves it with a reproducible negative/positive control pair rather than adding new source
